name: Jack Dorsey
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Twitter co-founding and first tweet were in March 2006 at age 29; Square launched later. Early dispatch programming and a 2000 Oakland dispatch startup are documented but not a clear material public breakthrough by the age-26 cutoff (Nov 2002).
early_history_summary: Born in St. Louis, Dorsey programmed dispatch routing from his teens, attended Missouri S&T then NYU (dropped out), and by 2000 was building web dispatch tools and sketching a status-message idea. He later joined Odeo and co-built Twitter in 2006.
family_context_summary: Born and raised in St. Louis; father worked with mass spectrometers, mother was a homemaker; raised Catholic.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father worked for a company that developed mass spectrometers; no strong documented domain transfer into social products.
evidence_summary: Dorsey’s defining public milestones—Twitter’s 2006 launch and Square—came after age 26. Pre-2003 activity centers on dispatch software and a small Oakland dispatch company without comparable material impact.

name: David Filo
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Jerry and David’s Guide / Yahoo directory began in February 1994 when Filo was 27 (born April 20, 1966); company incorporation and fame followed later.
early_history_summary: Born in Wisconsin and raised in Louisiana; BS computer engineering at Tulane, MS electrical engineering at Stanford (1990). Co-created a web directory with Jerry Yang as Stanford PhD students in 1994 that became Yahoo.
family_context_summary: Born in Wisconsin, raised in Moss Bluff, Louisiana. Family financial detail not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Filo’s defining milestone is co-creating Yahoo’s directory in February 1994 at age 27, past the age-26 cutoff. Earlier Stanford graduate work does not constitute a material independent milestone by 26.

name: Tobias Lütke
milestone_by_age_26: In 2004 co-launched Snowdevil, an online snowboard shop built on a custom Ruby on Rails e-commerce stack that the founders soon productized and relaunched as Shopify in 2006 (still at or under age 26).
early_history_summary: Born in Koblenz, Germany, Lütke received a computer at six, rewrote game code as a preteen, and left school after tenth grade for a programming apprenticeship. He moved to Canada around 2002–2003 and in 2004 built Snowdevil’s storefront himself in Rails when existing e-commerce software was inadequate.
family_context_summary: Born in Koblenz, West Germany; parents gave him a Schneider CPC computer at age six. Broader family wealth not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as industry insiders; early computer gift enabled self-taught programming.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early computer access, apprenticeship coding, Rails, Snowdevil cofounders, merchant pain
evidence_summary: Lütke’s path is heavy on self-taught technical depth from childhood hardware and game hacking, plus a German programming apprenticeship rather than elite university pipelines. Snowdevil (2004) forced him to build the store software that became Shopify; partners Scott Lake and Daniel Weinand provided complementary business/product capacity. Later in-laws (McKean family) were early Shopify investors, but that support followed the initial build rather than enabling the age-26 milestone.
starting_point: Born in Koblenz, Germany; early home computer access and a programming apprenticeship after leaving school post-tenth grade; emigrated to Canada in early 2000s.
current_position: CEO and co-founder of Shopify; multi-billion-dollar net worth; also competes in IMSA sports-car racing; Coinbase board member.

trajectory.event: Co-launched Snowdevil snowboard e-commerce site on a custom Rails stack with partners Lake and Weinand.
Pivoted the Snowdevil platform into Shopify as a multi-merchant e-commerce product.
Shopify went public; Lütke continued as CEO with dual-class control.
Received Canada’s Meritorious Service Cross for contributions to Canadian tech.
Joined Coinbase’s board of directors.
Continued as Shopify CEO while racing LMP2 in the IMSA SportsCar Championship.

name: Scott Farquhar
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Atlassian in 2002 with Mike Cannon-Brookes shortly after university, bootstrapping with credit-card debt and shipping Jira as a self-serve product.
early_history_summary: Born December 1979 in Parramatta, Sydney; attended selective James Ruse Agricultural High School and UNSW (Business Information Technology). Responded to Cannon-Brookes’s classmate email seeking a post-grad startup partner and co-founded Atlassian in 2002.
family_context_summary: Born in Parramatta, Sydney; father bought him an old computer for games, which sparked early tinkering. Not documented as wealthy.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father provided an early computer; no clear software-industry domain apprenticeship documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: James Ruse, UNSW Co-op, Cannon-Brookes partnership, bootstrap, Jira self-serve
evidence_summary: Farquhar’s early edge is institutional (top NSW selective school + UNSW BIT) plus an unusually durable cofounder bond with Cannon-Brookes. They bootstrapped Atlassian without VC until 2010, selling developer tools online rather than via a salesforce—riding open-source/agile tooling demand. Family background shows modest early computer access rather than capital or domain inheritance.
starting_point: Born December 1979 in Parramatta, Sydney; attended James Ruse Agricultural High School and UNSW on a technology scholarship path.
current_position: Atlassian co-founder and board member/special adviser after stepping down as co-CEO in 2024; multi-billionaire via Skip Capital and ~20% Atlassian stake.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Atlassian with Mike Cannon-Brookes, bootstrapping with credit-card debt.
Named EY Australian Entrepreneur of the Year with Cannon-Brookes.
Atlassian took first major external capital: $60M from Accel.
Atlassian IPO on Nasdaq; became one of Australia’s first tech billionaires.
Stepped down as co-CEO to focus on family, philanthropy, and tech ecosystem work; remained board adviser.

name: Mike Cannon-Brookes
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Atlassian in 2002 at about age 22 with Scott Farquhar after graduating UNSW; earlier sold student startup The Bookmark Box (2000).
early_history_summary: Born November 17, 1979 in Connecticut to a British banking executive father; lived in Taiwan and Hong Kong as a child, boarded in England, then Cranbrook School Sydney and UNSW BIT (co-op scholarship). Emailing classmates for a cofounder led to Farquhar and Atlassian in 2002.
family_context_summary: Son of a British global banking executive (also named Mike) and Helen; youngest of three; international childhood (Taiwan, Hong Kong, England boarding school) then elite Sydney private school Cranbrook.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a global banking executive—financial/professional platform rather than software domain expertise.
primary_early_advantage_tags: banking-executive family, Cranbrook, UNSW Co-op, Farquhar partnership, Bookmark Box
evidence_summary: Cannon-Brookes combined an internationally mobile, financially comfortable upbringing and elite Australian education with a high-trust cofounder partnership. Prior Bookmark Box sale showed early internet product instincts. Atlassian’s self-serve GTM and product focus defined their breakout more than inherited software networks.
starting_point: Born in Connecticut to a British banking executive father; raised across Taiwan, Hong Kong, and England boarding school before elite Sydney education.
current_position: Sole CEO of Atlassian (since Farquhar stepped down 2024); climate investor via Grok Ventures/Boundless Earth; multi-billionaire.

trajectory.event: Co-founded The Bookmark Box at university; sold to Blink.com.
Co-founded Atlassian with Scott Farquhar on credit-card bootstrap capital.
Named EY Australian Entrepreneur of the Year with Farquhar.
Atlassian IPO; became an Australian tech billionaire.
Became major AGL shareholder to accelerate decarbonisation; expanded climate investing.
Became sole Atlassian CEO after Farquhar stepped down as co-CEO.

name: Elizabeth Holmes
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Theranos (initially Real-Time Cures) in 2003 at age 19 while at Stanford, filed early patent applications, dropped out in 2004, and raised multi-million seed capital by late 2004.
early_history_summary: Born in Washington, D.C.; raised with strong elite-achievement expectations; studied Mandarin, attended St. John’s School (Houston) and Stanford chemical engineering. After a Genome Institute of Singapore summer, she founded a blood-testing company in 2003 and left Stanford to pursue it full-time.
family_context_summary: Father Christian Holmes IV held Enron-subsidiary and later USAID/EPA/USTDA executive roles; mother Noel was a Congressional staffer. Family lore emphasized Fleischmann’s Yeast fortune ancestry.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents provided high-status professional networks and achievement pressure more than direct biotech technical transfer; Tim Draper family connection aided first capital.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stanford, Silicon Valley, Draper capital, Channing Robertson, status family networks
evidence_summary: Holmes’s age-19 founding is independently dated across Wikipedia, Biography, and contemporary reporting. Early leverage was institutional (Stanford advisor Channing Robertson, SV geography) and network/capital (Tim Draper seed), not demonstrated blood-testing technical mastery—experts including Phyllis Gardner warned the science would not work. Later fraud convictions do not erase the dated founding milestone under the age-26 rule, but success_tier reflects eventual collapse rather than legendary durable achievement.
starting_point: Born in Washington, D.C. to a government/business executive father and Congressional staffer mother; family emphasized historic wealth ancestry and elite achievement.
current_position: Serving multi-year federal prison sentence after 2022 fraud convictions related to Theranos; reported release projection into early 2030s after later sentence reduction.

trajectory.event: Founded Real-Time Cures/Theranos and filed early wearable/drug-delivery patent applications while at Stanford.
Dropped out of Stanford; raised about $6M by year-end to fund Theranos.
Emerged from stealth with Walgreens partnership for store blood-draw centers.
Peak celebrity valuation era; WSJ investigation by John Carreyrou began exposing technology failures.
SEC fraud charges; federal criminal indictment of Holmes and Balwani; Theranos wound down.
Convicted on investor fraud counts and later sentenced to over 11 years in prison.
Began serving sentence at Federal Prison Camp, Bryan.

name: Andrej Karpathy
milestone_by_age_26: No material public milestone by age 26 found. By Oct 2012 (age 26) he was early in a Stanford PhD after U of Toronto (2009) and UBC master’s (2011) plus a 2011 Google Brain internship; OpenAI founding membership and PhD completion landed in 2015 at age 28–29.
early_history_summary: Born Bratislava (1986), moved to Toronto at 15; CS+Physics at University of Toronto; MSc UBC on simulated characters; Stanford PhD under Fei-Fei Li culminating 2015; then OpenAI founding research scientist and later Tesla Autopilot AI lead.
family_context_summary: Born in Bratislava, Czechoslovakia; family relocated to Toronto when he was 15. Parental occupations not detailed in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Strong early academic trajectory, but the independently famous milestones—OpenAI founding scientist, major vision-language papers era, CS231n, Tesla AI—cluster after age 26. Internships and degrees alone are not coded as material success milestones here.

name: Pieter Levels
milestone_by_age_26: No clear material milestone by age 26 found. Nomad List and the public “12 startups in 12 months” challenge were in 2014 when contemporary Wired coverage called him a 28-year-old Dutch programmer; earlier Panda Mix Show YouTube income is not a comparable dated product breakthrough under this rubric.
early_history_summary: Dutch indie maker; MBA background, self-taught coding; digital nomad who launched many bootstrapped products including Nomad List (2014) and Remote OK, later AI products such as PhotoAI.
family_context_summary: Described as middle-class Dutch upbringing; details thin in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Breakout indie products cluster around 2014 (~age 27–28). Without a better-dated ≤26 commercial milestone, he is coded ineligible despite later multi-million annual indie revenue.

name: Ryan Hoover
milestone_by_age_26: Launched Product Hunt on November 6, 2013 (initially an email list via Linkydink) while Director of Product at PlayHaven; it rapidly became a central tech product-discovery community and entered YC in 2014.
early_history_summary: Born in Eugene, Oregon to entrepreneurial parents who ran a video-game store where he worked as a child. University of Oregon business graduate; built a large personal writing/distribution habit (dozens to 150+ posts in 2013) before spinning Product Hunt from a side project into a company.
family_context_summary: Grew up in Eugene, Oregon; parents jointly ran small businesses including a video game store where Ryan worked as a child.
parent_family_domain_summary: Entrepreneurial parents and early exposure to video games/retail; not a Silicon Valley investor dynasty.
primary_early_advantage_tags: blogging distribution, product community, PlayHaven product role, YC later
evidence_summary: Product Hunt’s Nov 2013 launch is dated on Wikipedia and First Round Review; Hoover was ~26 (born 1987). Leverage was owned distribution from prolific blogging and deep product-manager immersion rather than elite school or family capital. Subsequent YC (2014), a16z Series A, and AngelList acquisition (~$20M, 2016) compounded after the age-26 milestone.
starting_point: Born in Eugene, Oregon to small-business parents who ran a video game store; early hands-on retail and gaming exposure.
current_position: Founder of Weekend Fund; former Product Hunt CEO (stepped down 2020); angel/early-stage investor.

trajectory.event: Launched Product Hunt as an email list that quickly became a product-discovery website.
Product Hunt joined Y Combinator and raised Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz.
AngelList acquired Product Hunt for about $20M.
Started Weekend Fund to invest in early-stage startups.
Stepped down as Product Hunt CEO.

name: Des Traynor
milestone_by_age_26: No clearly dated material milestone by age 26 found. Cofounder Eoghan McCabe’s contemporaneous account places Des at about age 30 when Intercom principles were written around the 2010–2011 founding; Exceptional (prior product) sale was 2011. CSV birth year 1986 conflicts with that first-person age pairing, so age-26 eligibility is not established.
early_history_summary: Irish product leader; co-founded design agency Contrast and error-tracking product Exceptional with McCabe and others, sold Exceptional in 2011, then co-founded Intercom (now Fin) as CSO/product leader.
evidence_summary: Without a reliable birth date reconciling to a ≤26 milestone, and with Intercom timing aligning to ~age 30 per cofounder narrative, Des is coded ineligible under strict rules.

name: Eoghan McCabe
milestone_by_age_26: Began building Intercom in late 2010/early 2011 at age ~26 (self-reported) after selling prior product Exceptional in 2011; Intercom formally launched with cofounders Des Traynor, Ciaran Lee, and David Barrett in 2011.
early_history_summary: Born Dublin 1984; first Geocities site ~1996; freelanced web work from ~16; Trinity College Dublin CS (face-tracker final project). Founded consulting firm then Contrast agency; built Exceptional crash monitoring, sold it in 2011, and redirected proceeds into Intercom.
family_context_summary: Dublin upbringing; parents initially could not afford a PC; father later bought a Packard Bell. Not an elite capital family; early internet access was hard-won.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as tech-domain parents; home computer arrived after pleading.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Trinity CS, teenage freelancing, Exceptional sale, Irish cofounder quartet, SF move
evidence_summary: McCabe’s own bio and First Round interview place Intercom’s start at age 26 after years of teenage freelancing and the Exceptional product. Material leverage is repeated SaaS building with a tight cofounder set and direct customer-messaging insight—not inherited Silicon Valley capital (seed was hard-fought). Later Intercom became a major B2B messenger/AI support platform; McCabe returned as CEO after a 2020–2022 hiatus.
starting_point: Born in Dublin in 1984 to a non-wealthy family; early fascination with PCs and the internet after limited home access.
current_position: CEO and co-founder of Fin (formerly Intercom), leading AI customer-service agent pivot; based in Bay Area.

trajectory.event: Graduated Trinity College Dublin CS and founded Eoghan McCabe Limited consulting practice.
Wrote first Intercom code in late 2010 after building Contrast/Exceptional with Irish peers.
Sold Exceptional; raised ~$1M seed and launched Intercom full-time with three cofounders.
Intercom reached unicorn-scale valuation era after rapid SMB messenger growth.
Stepped aside as CEO amid health and board turmoil; later returned in 2022.
Drove AI-first reboot culminating in Fin AI agent as core growth product.

name: Mathilde Collin
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Front in 2013 (about age 24) with Laurent Perrin, building a shared inbox/customer communication platform; company later became a unicorn.
early_history_summary: Born April 20, 1989 in France; father engineer, mother executive assistant; grandparents farmers/masons. HEC Paris entrepreneurship track; left traditional path to found Front in Paris in 2013 with technical cofounder Perrin and early advice/support from entrepreneur Thibaud Elzière, then scaled in SF.
family_context_summary: French middle-class professional family: engineer father, executive-assistant mother; grandparents in agriculture and construction trades.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an engineer—general technical household, not SaaS/inbox domain experts.
primary_early_advantage_tags: HEC Paris, technical cofounder Perrin, Elzière mentorship, shared-inbox wave
evidence_summary: French Wikipedia and company histories date Front’s 2013 founding when Collin was 24. HEC entrepreneurship training, a complementary technical cofounder, and early operator mentorship mattered more than family capital. Front later raised large rounds and reached ~$1.7B valuation (2022), placing her as a notable SaaS founder rather than global tier-1 icon.
starting_point: Born in France in 1989 to an engineer father and executive-assistant mother; grandparent generation in trades/farming.
current_position: Co-founder and Executive Chair of Front (stepped from CEO ~2024); angel investor; company previously valued around $1.7B.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Front in Paris with Laurent Perrin to rebuild shared team inboxes.
Scaled Front with venture funding and US market expansion.
Front raised Series D at ~$1.7B valuation, entering unicorn status.
Moved from CEO to Executive Chair while remaining co-founder.
